analysis:
The changed files, docs/developer/test.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md, are documentation only. No executable code, protocol, key-handling, attestation or authorization logic changes in this batch.

What the docs now describe:
- A new add-on hold feature. `darkbloom addon` offers `status`, `hold` and `release [--force]`, with an AF_UNIX socket at `~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock` (0600, 0700 directory), `addon-hold.json` (0600) and an `ownership.lock`. The CLI reaches the provider through an owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to the live process identity.
- Documented behavior: a hold closes admission, drains accepted work for up to 120 s and unloads all models, which affects availability only. `release --force` is allowed even while an add-on holds the machine lock.
- The test doc (docs/developer/test.md lines 768-790) says the real peer policy is exercised only negatively, because no signed add-on is available to the test runner. A test authenticator stands in for it in the socket and serve-loop flows. Physical add-on interoperation is a separate check.

Security-relevant points for later passes:
- New local attack surface: a socket-based IPC trust boundary where a local process could hold or drain the provider (a DoS vector, related to T-016 and T-029 in kind). Peer authentication is described as a peer policy, but the implementation is not in this batch. Its strength cannot be verified here, and positive-path peer authentication is untested per the docs. This is a threat-model gap to track, not a finding, since there is no code evidence.
- The `hold` command carries a lease of 30-600 s, which bounds the DoS window per the docs. `release --force` can end a hold while add-on VMs still use memory. That is an operator action by the same user.
- The change does not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract, prompt confidentiality (A-001), the X25519 key (A-003), App Attest authorization (A-016) or the prefix cache (T-041). The docs say a held provider keeps its connection and sends draining heartbeats with no `provider_drain`, so the coordinator-side semantics need platform review.

No regression is identified from documentation alone. The add-on implementation files (AddonHoldPaths, ProviderLoop+AddonHold, the peer policy) are outside the supplied evidence.
